why: ci/negative_control_cleanroom_redaction.py needs the REAL bytes of the two rejected
revisions of python/verify_cleanroom.py to prove today's privacy suite is
load-bearing. Reaching them through `git show <branch-sha>` made the control depend
on commits that no landing preserves: this repository allows only squash and rebase
(allow_merge_commit: false) and deletes the branch on merge, and CI's fetch-depth: 0
never fetches a deleted PR head. The control then loses every REPLAYED arm on the
first push to main and reports FAIL(condition=arm_did_not_fire) forever.
These files ARE the evidence, committed in the tree, bound by content digest. They
replay identically on a branch, on a squash, on a rebase, on a cherry-pick and in a
fresh main-only clone, because nothing about them mentions a commit.

digest.over: the file's bytes with CRLF newlines normalised to LF
why_normalised: this repository is developed with core.autocrlf=true on Windows and checked out
with LF on Linux CI. A digest over raw checkout bytes would be a platform test,
not an integrity test. `.gitattributes` additionally marks this directory -text so
the checkout is byte-stable, and the normalisation makes the binding hold even in

how_to_add_a_fixture: 1. Write the file with the exact bytes to replay, LF-terminated.
2. Add an entry here with its sha256 (LF-normalised) and, in `carries`, the defects
it is being kept for. Every `carries` entry must be reproduced by a named arm in
ci/negative_control_cleanroom_redaction.py -- a fixture whose defect no arm
demonstrates is a file nobody would notice going stale.
3. `origin` is provenance for a human reader ONLY. Nothing in the control resolves
it, and the control must stay green in a clone where it cannot resolve.

origin.note: PR #57 revision 1, the head of the first rejection (issue #55 B1/B2/B3). Provenance only.

carries: B1: _echo_cmd gates on `"://" in s`, so a scheme-relative or schemeless credential URL is echoed raw
B2: main() calls _scrub_text(install.stderr[-1500:], url) -- truncate before scrub, so a straddling credential survives
B3: _redact_url_userinfo leaves query and fragment credentials untouched

origin.note: PR #57 revision 2, the head of the second rejection (R2/R3). Provenance only.

carries: R2: _echo_cmd scans generally and never sees the run's own raw --index-url, so a schemeless URL whose credential is in the query or fragment is echoed raw while the record redacts the identical input

R3: the scanner's schemeless `@`-gated alternative rewrites ordinary Windows paths -- C:\Users\justin.chu@contoso.com\... becomes REDACTED@contoso.com\..., in the echoed argv AND in record['venv'] / record['wheel'] / registered_path
R3b: the same alternative rewrites a bare e-mail address in ordinary prose
N1: _sanitize_urls_in_text is not idempotent -- a second pass over already-sanitised text rewrites it again
